tier_reason: C stands: the S&P 2020 paper is still unreachable (nebelwelt.net and cs.purdue.edu fail DNS), so the numbers remain abstract snippets.

corrections.workload: Binary-only AddressSanitizer (BASan) and AFL coverage instrumentation inserted by static rewriting of x86_64 and aarch64 Linux binaries, versus Valgrind memcheck, source-level ASan and QEMU-mode AFL on SPEC CPU2006 C benchmarks and fuzzing targets.
corrections.tradeoffs: The x64 rewriter needs non-stripped position-independent (PIE) binaries; the aarch64 rewriter uses a different algorithm and handles stripped and non-PIE binaries. C++ support is unfinished on both architectures (issue #26 open). The tool itself is Python, but its output is ordinary assembler, so rewritten binaries are usable in C++ workflows.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the 3x is against Valgrind memcheck, which checks different things (it also tracks uninitialised values), so it is not a like-for-like sanitizer comparison; the abstract snippet puts BASan about 0.65x slower than source-level ASan on SPEC2006 C, and a Purdue thesis snippet gives 7.5x for AFL over QEMU where the abstract says 4.5x. The x64 BASan pass skips memory operands that are not 1, 2, 4 or 8 bytes, so 16-byte SSE/AVX accesses go unchecked, and it adds stack redzones only to functions that load a stack canary. Open issue #49: BASan-rewritten SPEC2006 gcc and bzip2 segfault on x64, with no maintainer reply. 29 open issues, last commit 2025-04-26.

tier_reason: C stands: competitor-run 2015-2016 spdlog table with a tuned Easylogging++ configuration.

corrections.tradeoffs: Two source files (easylogging++.h plus easylogging++.cc, single-header only in v9.7x and older), many features (custom sinks, performance tracking, hierarchical loggers, macros that define global state). Configuration macros such as ELPP_THREAD_SAFE must be passed as compiler flags so easylogging++.cc sees them (issue #590). Repo archived read-only on 2025-07-06; its own README now recommends spdlog for new projects. Heavy macro and global-state design.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the earlier note that both libraries write with mostly default buffering is wrong for Easylogging++: by default it flushes after every entry and echoes every line to stdout, and the bench turned both off (Log_Flush_Threshold 10,485,760 entries, so no flush during the run; TO_STANDARD_OUTPUT false), so a tuned configuration was measured against a default glog. The _ELPP_ macros show v9.75 or older was measured (v9.80 drops the underscore). glog at 100 threads (1.139 s) beat glog at 10 threads (3.032 s), an unexplained inversion with no run script or repeat data. Open, unanswered issues include a disk-full rolling deadlock (#744) and a multi-threaded performance-tracking crash (#790).

tier_reason: C stands: first-party coverage table in AFL's own technical notes.

corrections.tradeoffs: Needs an instrumented target (afl-gcc, afl-clang or the LLVM plugin; QEMU mode for black-box binaries is about 2-5x slower than compile-time instrumentation) and takes input as a file; persistent and deferred modes need small code changes and care to reset state. Archived and read-only; llvm_mode is reported broken with LLVM/Clang 13 (open issues #151, #156). The maintained community fork is AFL++ (release 5.03c); its default licence is now AGPL-3.0-or-later, while code compiled into the fuzzing harness stays Apache-2.0.
corrections.caveats: Enricher: the docs do not say how blocks and edges were counted, and the guided runs took longer than 'Blind fuzzing L', so the coverage comparison is not at equal wall time. The speed claims (LLVM mode up to about 2x, fork server 1.5x-2x, deferred fork server 10x+) are prose ratios against AFL's own slower modes, not against another fuzzer. AFL is a fuzzer, not a profiler, so it fits its category loosely.
